title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Citrix confirms two NetScaler zero-days exploited before patching, CVSS 9.5; CISA KEV deadline is 30 September
items.content_text: Citrix confirmed on 27 September that two NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws, CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS 9.5 each), were exploited before patches existed. The first lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands in any configuration; the second is a DTLS memory-overflow reachable on VPN virtual servers, where DTLS is on by default. Fixes shipped the same day in 14.1-73.37 and 13.1-64.23, and CISA added both flaws to KEV with a 30 September federal deadline. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 exposed instances, and no actor or victim has been named. For manufacturers the concern is the front door: NetScaler Gateway commonly fronts contractor, integrator and remote-engineer access into plant DMZs. Because exploitation preceded disclosure, patching alone does not show whether an appliance was already compromised, and Citrix warns its IOC scan does not cover every technique.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Citrix security bulletin CTX697096, 27 Sep 2026 (primary); CISA KEV, 27 Sep 2026; Cybersecurity Dive and Unit 42, 28 Sep 2026
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Exploited pre-disclosure; patched 27 Sep 2026; more than 20,000 instances exposed per Shadowserver

items.title: Microsoft: a ransomware affiliate rotating Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT lists critical manufacturing among 14 targeted sectors
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a profile on 24 September of Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate that deploys Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis or BERT while its hands-on tradecraft stays the same. Microsoft lists 14 affected sectors, including critical manufacturing, chemicals, energy, and food and agriculture, and names no victims. It says how the group gets in remains unconfirmed. Once inside, the affiliate relies on remote-management tools (Atera, MeshAgent, ScreenConnect, Splashtop), scanning and PsExec, credential theft with Mimikatz, LaZagne and ntdsutil, Rclone or s5cmd to move data out, and Cloudflared or ngrok for tunnelling. Black Kite’s count through July puts Qilin first and DragonForce fourth among ransomware groups hitting manufacturers, so this playbook overlaps with the most active brands against the sector.
tags: Ransomware — Multi-brand affiliate tradecraft, initial access unconfirmed

items.title: Boston Scientific confirms an intruder reached an external-facing network device and stopped manufacturing; SCADA systems were not reached
items.content_text: Boston Scientific disclosed on 25–26 August that a cyber incident had disrupted its network and business applications, hurting its ability to manufacture and to process and ship orders. In a 22 September update, the company said CrowdStrike’s investigation found the actor gained access to an external-facing network device and then to a limited part of its on-premises IT environment, with no evidence of compromise in manufacturing-maintenance, product and software development, medical-device maintenance or SCADA systems, and no evidence of data being staged or exfiltrated from those systems. An 8-K filed in early September said most facilities had resumed manufacturing and that the incident would materially affect 2026 results; revised guidance is due on the 28 October earnings call. The case shows an IT-side compromise of one internet-facing device can stop production without control systems ever being touched.
tags: Incident — Confirmed IT breach stopped manufacturing; no SCADA compromise found

_otthreatfeed.category: Incident — Confirmed IT breach stopped manufacturing; no SCADA compromise found

items.title: Ransomware hit a 2026 high in August with industrial firms taking 31% of incidents, and a new group, Aurora, is abusing VPN access
items.content_text: NCC Group’s August review counts 1,073 ransomware incidents, up 12% from July and the highest month of 2026, with industrials (a broader class than manufacturing alone) taking 329, or 31%, up from 28% in July. Qilin led with 15% of incidents, and North America took 44% of the total. NCC also profiles Aurora, a new 2026 group that exploits VPN vulnerabilities against manufacturing, legal and research targets; in one August transportation case it encrypted hypervisors while also extorting for stolen data. Black Kite’s 18 September report is consistent: 1,183 manufacturing victims through July, up 39.7% year over year, with Qilin (178), The Gentlemen (142), Akira (96), DragonForce (70) and INC Ransom (65) leading and 70.2% of victims earning $10–100 million a year.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: NCC Group monthly threat review, 23 Sep 2026 (primary); covered by Industrial Cyber, 28 Sep 2026; Black Kite report, 18 Sep 2026
_otthreatfeed.date_note: August 2026 data; Black Kite data through Jul 2026

items.title: Forescout: an AI model ported a pre-authentication PLC exploit between WAGO models in about 8.5 hours, but needed heavy human guidance
items.content_text: Forescout’s Vedere Labs reported on 1 September that it used Claude to adapt an exploit for CVE-2021-31886, a pre-authentication stack overflow (CVSS 9.8) in the Nucleus FTP server, from the WAGO 750-852 PLC to the 750-831, reaching ARM shellcode execution without credentials. The final stage took 8 hours 32 minutes and $535.74 in API usage, needed human researchers to steer past dead ends, and a follow-on attempt at a command-and-control implant permanently damaged the test device. The Hacker News, citing CERT@VDE, reports no update exists for affected models on the Nucleus V1 firmware. Forescout’s point is that AI lowers the cost of exploit work on embedded controllers, not that it removes the need for skill. Context, 20 August: CISA, NSA and the FBI warned that unattributed actors are using AI-generated scripts against exposed Siemens S7 PLCs, with no single patch.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Research (Vedere Labs), 1 Sep 2026 (primary); The Hacker News, 2 Sep 2026; CISA/NSA/FBI S7 advisory, 20 Aug 2026 (context)

items.title: Nozomi finds 19 flaws in a Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link master, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass that chains to root
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks Labs published research on 24 September describing 19 vulnerabilities in the web management interface of the Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 IO-Link master (EtherNet/IP firmware 1.7.3). The worst, CVE-2026-27546 (CVSS 9.8), lets an unauthenticated attacker obtain an admin session; chained with OS command injection flaws (CVSS 8.8) that run as root, it gives full control of the device, and an unauthenticated path-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-27557, CVSS 7.5) exposes SSH keys. Pepperl+Fuchs fixed the issues through coordinated disclosure with CERT@VDE (VDE-2026-014), and a Security Boulevard summary of the research points to firmware 1.7.8. No exploitation is reported. IO-Link masters bridge sensors and actuators on a machine to the plant’s EtherNet/IP network, so a compromised master is a foothold inside the cell.

items.title: Schneider’s Modicon M580, a mainstay of process plants, has a critical authentication flaw (CVSS v4.0 9.2)
items.content_text: Schneider Electric’s September ICS Patch Tuesday included CVE-2026-3869, a critical authentication flaw (CWE-303, incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm) in the Modicon M580 and M580 Safety controllers, scored 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, according to SecurityWeek on 9 September. Blastwave’s write-up lists affected firmware as M580 below application level 4.00, M580 Safety below 4.20 and the MC80, under Schneider advisory SEVD-2026-251-04; confirm ranges in Schneider’s own advisory. No exploitation is reported, and the score assumes an attacker can already reach the controller network. M580 CPUs run continuous processes where firmware changes wait for planned outages, so segmentation and access control carry the risk until you can patch.

items.title: Rockwell publishes nine advisories at once, covering ControlLogix, CompactLogix, RSLinx Classic, FactoryTalk Historian and ControlFLASH
items.content_text: Rockwell Automation released nine security advisories on 1 September (SD1792 to SD1800), each rated High on its portal. They cover CompactLogix 5380 and ControlLogix 5580 controllers, RSLinx Classic, FactoryTalk Historian Machine Edition, FactoryTalk Activation Manager, ControlFLASH, the 1756-ENBT module, ArmorStart LT motor controllers and the Redundancy Module Configuration Tool. SecurityWeek (2 September) singles out four critical or high denial-of-service flaws in RSLinx Classic and the Logix denial-of-service flaw CVE-2026-9637, for which CISA says it is not aware of exploitation. RSLinx Classic and ControlFLASH run on engineering workstations, so the advisories matter most where those hosts can be reached from the business network.

items.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting duties took effect on 11 September: manufacturers must report exploited product vulnerabilities within 24 hours
items.content_text: Since 11 September, manufacturers of products with digital elements sold in the EU must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting product security, according to the European Commission. The steps are an early warning within 24 hours, a fuller notification within 72 hours, and a final report no later than 14 days after a fix is available (for vulnerabilities) or one month after the 72-hour notification (for incidents). Reports go once through a single reporting platform run by ENISA, which became operational on 11 September, and the receiving national CSIRT shares them with the others. For machine builders and component makers that put controllers, HMIs, gateways and connected equipment on the EU market, this turns vulnerability handling into a legal deadline; for plant owners, expect supplier notifications on this timetable.

items.title: CISA and the FBI tell operators to rein in third-party ICS integrators after a 2025 integrator breach exposed customer SCADA files
items.content_text: CISA and the FBI published joint guidance on 24 September for critical infrastructure operators working with third-party ICS integrators. It draws on a March–April 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation company in which a foreign actor searched for “customers” and “SCADA” and staged about 800 files of customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics in nine archives. The agencies urge contract security requirements, least privilege, monitored and on-demand remote access, a full inventory of integrator-supplied equipment, offline backups and the ability to operate manually if the integrator is compromised. The victim’s named customers were power and transportation entities, not manufacturers, but plants routinely give OEMs, machine builders and integrators standing access to PLCs, robots and MES interfaces. Separately, NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Rev. 4, its OT security guide, on 21 September, restructured around CSF 2.0; comments are due 30 November.
tags: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrators; NIST OT security guide draft
